Your AI chatbot never actually sees the letters in your words.
Most language models first chop text into tokens, little word fragments, before they read anything.
So a word like strawberry can arrive as a few chunks. Counting its letters turns into guessing.
On October 7th, a Nature paper showed another way: let the model read raw bytes.
A byte is the smallest piece a computer stores. Every letter, symbol and line of code is made of them.
Byte models existed, but they lagged behind. Too many tiny pieces, and too slow.
The fix is called byteification. Take an existing token model, and retrofit it in two stages, with little extra training.
The result approaches token models, and does better where single characters matter.
Think computer code, or DNA, where one character can change the whole meaning.
